verdict.rationale: Unity ships an official, first-party Unity CLI for installing and managing Editors and modules, aimed at automation and CI where the full Hub is unwanted (unity-docs-25/26/33/34, unity-probe-5). A runtime probe confirms an agent-oriented design: a keyless install script, Homebrew/deb/rpm/MSIX packages, structured JSON/TSV output, documented exit codes, its own llms.txt, and `unity <command>`/`unity eval` built for agents that run shell commands, plus a `unity mcp` mode (unity-probe-rt-4). Editor and Player command-line arguments are also documented for headless operation (unity-docs-6/7/8). Missing for 10: the CLI is still labelled experimental, and there is no independent community or hands-on report of AI agents using it in practice.
